L31·N967unmasked layer
This neuron fires on delimiter/boundary punctuation rather than content — paragraph-break newlines (e.g. right after a heading or question) and opening quote/parenthesis/apostrophe/bracket/hyphen tokens that introduce an inset literal or quoted term (' 'im', ' (->)', '[at]', 'people-pleasing'); notably the same token types (opening "(" of an explanatory parenthetical, opening “, some newlines) drive it strongly negative, so it is a sign-coded punctuation-boundary detector, not a semantic one.

L31·N2753unmasked layer
This neuron's real signal is its large negative activation: it fires (strongly negative) on the token immediately preceding a **female** given name — typically after feminine cues like "her", "wife", "sister", "niece" or the comma introducing a woman's name — whereas the same pre-name slot before **male** names (e.g. "man Dave", "while Josh", "Mr." before a man's surname) stays near zero/positive; i.e. it encodes "the upcoming person name is female".

L31·N4989unmasked layer
Fires on continuation pieces inside titles, proper-name strings and list enumerations — e.g. the "&"/comma joining items in a book title or "Makers, hackers, artists…", sub-word fragments of rare proper nouns (Sah-**ar**-awis, Pter-**am**-ander), and digits/spaces inside dates and durations; it is suppressed on ordinary function words like " a" and " past".
